newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian newspaper says 1996 was "dark year".
newsitem.headline: Syrian newspaper says 1996 was "dark year".

text.p: Goodbye and good riddance to 1996, an official Syrian newspaper declared on Tuesday, calling it a "dark year" for Middle East peace.

"By all standards, 1996 was an unhappy year, a dark year with few faint lights here and there. The good thing about it is that is cannot be repeated. It has gone for ever," columnist Fouad Mardoud said in the English-language Syria Times.

The newspaper, reflecting the Syrian government's view, pinned the blame firmly at the door of Israel and its election last May of Benjamin Netanyahu whose right-wing government has rejected the land-for-peace formula that had formed the basis of peace talks since 1991.
"The big story of the passing year was the current deep recess of the Middle East peace process created by the Israeli government of Netanyahu which was the product of that dark year," Mardoud said.
He urged U.S. President Bill Clinton, who starts a new term in 1997, to put pressure on Netanyahu to accept a peace deal with Damascus.
Israel's previous government broke off talks with Syria last March after a spate of suicide bombings by Islamic militants.
"The current stalemate of the peace talks appears headed for a dangerous and possibly bursting situation. Mr Netanyahu has not given up endeavoring to stop the negotiations," Mardoud said.
